messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>

Cc: Anna Cole <anna.cole@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Dec 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Close window drift: stabilization plan and procurement handoff

Team —

Quick note: Acme has signaled a 3-week shift to their internal evaluation window (procurement + security gating). That pushes our target close from 2025-12-18 to ~2026-01-08 unless we intervene. I captured a short risk registry and a proposed stabilization sequence in the attached MAP-v3 (PDF).

Immediate asks:
- Karthik: can you validate the reduced-scope canary we can commit to while procurement finishes? I sketched two fallback options in the MAP (page 3).
- Grace: please open a procurement triage with Anna and request a firm date and any additional audit artifacts they need.

Why this matters: if we let the window slip without a staged acceptance, the probability of competing vendor re-evaluation rises and our renewal cadence with Acme shrinks. We should both try to rebaseline and create a short-term acceptance lane to lock the initial payment terms.

Attachments: MAP-v3-AcmeHealth-2025-11-30.pdf (proposal), procurement-checklist-acme.xlsx (artifact tracker)

Thanks —
Mina

Subject: Re: Close window drift: stabilization plan and procurement handoff

Thanks Mina — clear and urgent. Quick notes after a first pass through the MAP:

1) Canary option validation
- Option A (feature-limited canary) looks doable: we can lock a 2-node dedicated pool and expose the same API surface with token caps. Latency SLOs will be relaxed to 200ms 95th for the first 2 weeks.
- Option B (behavioral canary) requires an extra eval run; that will add ~5 business days.

2) Risk sizing
- If procurement delays > 2 weeks, our unit economics worsen by ~9% due to longer warmers and reserved capacity. Put a soft cap in the MAP for cost-absorption and get exec approval if exceeded.

3) Next steps for me
- I'll send a lightweight SOW appendix (1 page) to make the acceptance criteria explicit — target EOD Tue.

Will coordinate with SRE on the reserve. Karthik

Team / Execs —

Update after Anna's note: procurement freeze to 12/22 is confirmed. Acme can accept a limited-feature pilot if we supply the audit bundle and an appendix that caps traffic. Given the slide we have two choices: 1) accept the three-week drift and keep the original commercial terms but risk competitive re-evals; or 2) sign the pilot appendix and absorb up to $12k in marginal cost for reserved warmers to protect the close (see cost tab in procurement-checklist-acme.xlsx).

I'm asking for approval to pursue option 2 and sign the one-page appendix (draft attached) to secure the pilot lane and initial payment. If execs prefer not to absorb incremental cost, we'll proceed with rebaseline messaging and a new target close of 2026-01-08.

Decision requested by Monday EOD (2025-12-08) so we can get the appendix to Acme before their holiday freeze.
